text: Working with APIs is an essential skill for modern developers. An API allows two programs to communicate, usually through HTTP requests such as GET or POST. When you send a request, the server often returns data in JSON format, which is easy to read and parse. Most APIs require authentication, for example an API key or token, to verify who you are. It is also important to respect rate limits, which restrict how many requests you can make in a certain time. Finally, good error handling helps you deal with problems like network failures or invalid responses, making your application more reliable.
